prompt: Write a blog post about this year's Christmas drama rehearsals at my church. I auditioned for a lead role but got cast as a side character instead. I was a bit disappointed at first, but ended up really enjoying building a backstory for the character anyway. One funny moment: during dress rehearsal I completely forgot my one line, panicked for a second, and just improvised something on the spot -- and it actually worked better dramatically than the scripted line. The director laughed about it afterward and said to keep it in.
assertions: Opens with a hook rather than throat-clearing scene-setting
Admits the initial disappointment about not getting the lead role plainly, without over-apologizing or excessive hedging
Contains at least one H2 header phrased as a question
Includes the improvised-line anecdote with concrete specific detail (not vague summary)
Ending is a genuine reflective callback rather than a generic 'moral of the story' wrap-up
Does not contain banned buzzwords or fake-profound kicker phrasing invented beyond what's in the material
Uses short paragraphs and at least one deliberate fragment or ellipsis for emphasis
